input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-readiness assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's core unknown: the full inventory of gaps
between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar for Llama Stack. It
produces the definitive GA scope that all stability and hardening work is
sized against. Until this assessment lands, the size of the GA work is an
estimate (the strategy's only open question).

## Scope

- Inventory gaps between current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar across
  the four areas named by the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale
  limits, and error handling.
- Consolidate Tech Preview feedback scattered across support tickets into the
  gap inventory.
- For each gap, record severity, the delta to the GA bar, and the affected
  surface (API, distribution, operator).
- Produce the definitive GA scope: a prioritized list of gaps that must close
  for GA, mapped to work areas (API stability work, support posture work), so
  each downstream workstream can be sized.
- Identify gaps that are already met and need only verification evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written GA-readiness assessment exists that inventories gaps across API
  stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling, with each gap
  assigned a severity and a GA-bar delta.
- Tech Preview feedback from support tickets is reviewed and represented in
  the gap inventory (each ticket theme either maps to a gap or is explicitly
  dispositioned as not GA-blocking).
- The assessment outputs a definitive GA scope list, with each scope item
  mapped to a downstream work area (API stability, support posture, or
  already-met/verify-only).
- The API stability and support posture workstreams can be sized from the
  assessment: each relevant scope item carries an effort estimate or size
  range.
- Every gap in the inventory is either in the GA scope, dispositioned as
  deferred with rationale, or marked already-met with the verification
  evidence needed.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is that
  assessment.

# API stability guarantees: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, TP upgrade path

## Description

This epic puts a stability guarantee on Llama Stack's published API surface so
enterprise customers can build production GenAI applications against it: the
API surface becomes versioned, a deprecation policy is published and enforced,
and a tested upgrade path exists from the last two Tech Preview releases. The
specific gaps to close are defined by the GA-readiness assessment.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution (the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution-facing surfaces),
  per the versioning approach the team selects.
- Publish and enforce a deprecation policy for the versioned API surface:
  how changes are announced, how long deprecated surfaces remain supported,
  and how clients are expected to migrate.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases
  to the GA release, including the distribution/operator upgrade mechanics.
- Close the API-stability and error-handling gaps that the GA-readiness
  assessment places in this workstream's scope (e.g., consistent error
  responses on the versioned surface).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface carries explicit version identifiers, and the
  versioning scheme is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published, and any API change made in this epic
  follows it (deprecated surfaces remain available for the policy's support
  window).
- The upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview releases is tested
  and evidenced: a repeatable upgrade procedure exists and passes against a
  representative distribution configuration, including data/CR migration where
  applicable.
- Clients written against the Tech Preview API surface continue to function
  within the deprecation policy's compatibility window (no unannounced
  breaking changes).
- All API-stability and error-handling gaps assigned to this workstream by the
  GA-readiness assessment are closed or explicitly deferred with rationale in
  the assessment's tracking artifact.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee:
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic is
  gated on that assessment, with re-scope expected rather than exceptional.
  If the assessment finds the API surface already substantially meets the
  bar, this epic narrows to deprecation-policy publication and upgrade-path
  testing only.
- Re-split trigger: if the assessment's API-stability scope exceeds one
  sprint of estimated effort for this workstream, re-split along the
  assessment's gap categories (e.g., API versioning/deprecation policy vs.
  upgrade-path implementation and testing) so no epic exceeds the ~2-week
  guideline.

# Production support posture: SLOs, backport policy, supported configuration matrix

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for Llama Stack
GA: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a validated supported
configuration matrix. It is the "can Red Hat support this in production"
workstream, distinct from the API surface work — different deliverables
(policy documents and a validated matrix) and a different review cycle.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack distribution
  (service-level objectives for the supported deployment model, as defined by
  the team in line with platform support standards).
- Define and document the backport policy: which release lines receive fixes
  and for how long, aligned with the platform's support policy.
- Define the supported configuration matrix: the distribution configurations
  (deployment topologies, provider combinations, platform versions) that are
  supported at GA.
- Validate the matrix: run verification against each declared supported
  configuration so the matrix ships as tested fact, not aspiration.
- Include the TrustyAI guardrails integration configuration in the matrix
  once it is promoted to supported status in the GA distribution: the
  promotion and its end-to-end evidence land in the distribution-side
  guardrails work this epic is sequenced after, and this epic verifies the
  configuration and records the evidence in the matrix entry.
- Fold in the scale-limit and error-handling gap outcomes from the GA
  readiness assessment where they belong to support posture (documented
  limits, support escalation paths).

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA distribution are documented and published in the
  support-posture artifact.
- The backport policy is documented, covering supported release lines and
  fix-backport rules.
- The supported configuration matrix is published, and every configuration it
  declares as supported has passed a verification run with recorded evidence.
- No configuration is listed as supported without verification evidence; any
  configuration that fails verification is listed as unsupported or removed,
  with the failure recorded.
- The TrustyAI guardrails integration configuration is included in the
  published matrix as supported, with verification evidence recorded from a
  run against the promoted integration.
- Support-posture gaps assigned to this workstream by the GA-readiness
  assessment are closed or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

## Risks / Notes

- SLO targets and backport policy require product/support-organization
  sign-off — budget review time from stakeholders outside the engineering
  team.
- Scope is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic is
  gated on that assessment. If the assessment finds existing platform support
  standards already cover part of the posture, this epic narrows to
  Llama-Stack-specific SLOs and matrix validation.
- Re-split trigger: if the assessment places more support-posture scope in
  this workstream than one sprint of estimated effort (beyond SLO/backport
  policy definition and matrix validation), re-split along the assessment's
  gap categories (policy definition vs. matrix validation runs) so no epic
  exceeds the ~2-week guideline.

# Promote TrustyAI guardrails integration to supported status in Llama Stack distributions

## Description

This epic makes safety guardrails via TrustyAI a supported, documented
integration for GA Llama Stack distributions, instead of an experimental
flag-gated option. Enterprise GA customers get guardrails as part of the
supported distribution, not as an opt-in experiment.

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration from the current experimental
  flag-gated state to a supported integration in the GA Llama Stack
  distribution, following the existing provider/safety-plugin wiring pattern.
- Ensure the integration works with the distribution's supported deployment
  model (TrustyAIService instances per project acting as the guardrails
  provider for Llama Stack distributions).
- Exercise the integration against the guardrails use cases the GA bar
  requires (requests routed through the safety provider, policy outcomes
  enforced) on a representative configuration.
- Document the integration from the distribution side: what is supported,
  how it is enabled and configured, and its supported state as an entry in
  the supported configuration matrix, together with the end-to-end
  verification evidence that entry requires. The matrix itself is published
  and verified in the support-posture workstream, which is sequenced after
  this epic so the guardrails entry and its evidence are in place before the
  matrix ships. (This documentation is the engineering-source reference for
  the integration; user-facing documentation is authored separately through
  the Red Hat docs content process.)
- Provide a disable/rollback path: the integration can be turned off via
  distribution configuration without breaking the rest of the distribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack distribution can be configured with TrustyAI guardrails
  without any experimental/Tech Preview opt-in flag.
- The integration is exercised end to end on a representative supported
  configuration: requests subject to guardrails policies produce the expected
  enforcement outcomes, with recorded evidence.
- The integration is documented as supported, including enablement and
  configuration guidance.
- The integration's supported state is declared for the supported
  configuration matrix with the recorded end-to-end evidence, so the
  support-posture matrix entry for the guardrails configuration can be
  published and verified from this epic's deliverables.
- The integration can be disabled via configuration, and a distribution with
  the integration disabled otherwise functions normally (rollback path).
- Any GA-bar requirements the guardrails integration must meet for supported
  status (error behavior, upgrade behavior) are verified and recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# TrustyAI-side validation of the guardrails integration for GA distributions

## Description

The TrustyAI team validates that the TrustyAI guardrails service is a
supported integration target for GA Llama Stack distributions: the service
side of the integration is verified, version-compatibility expectations are
documented, and any service-side adjustments needed for supported status are
made. TrustyAI itself is already a Stable (GA) component — this epic is the
different-team validation of a passive component becoming an actively
supported integration point.

## Scope

- Validate the TrustyAI guardrails service against the Llama Stack
  distribution integration: the supported TrustyAIService configurations that
  can back a Llama Stack distribution's guardrails provider, exercised
  together with the distribution-side integration.
- Verify version compatibility between the TrustyAI service releases and the
  GA Llama Stack distribution, and document the supported combinations.
- Record validation evidence: guardrails policies enforced through the
  integration, service behavior under distribution load and error conditions
  relevant to the GA bar.
- Make any TrustyAI-side adjustments required for the integration to be
  supported (service behavior, documentation of the integration contract from
  the TrustyAI side), if validation surfaces them.
- Document TrustyAI-side integration requirements (provisioning, sizing,
  supported TrustyAIService settings) for customers using the integration —
  as the TrustyAI-side engineering-source reference; the user-facing
  documentation is authored separately through the Red Hat docs content
  process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering the guardrails integration scenarios
  exercised jointly with the distribution-side integration, with
  pass/fail results recorded.
- Supported version combinations (TrustyAI service × Llama Stack
  distribution) are documented, and each declared combination has validation
  evidence.
- Guardrails enforcement through the integration is verified: policies
  configured on the TrustyAI service produce the expected outcomes for
  requests routed from a Llama Stack distribution.
- TrustyAI-side integration documentation exists, covering provisioning and
  supported settings for the integration.
- Any TrustyAI-side issues found during validation are either fixed or
  recorded with disposition (supported workaround or documented limitation).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions — the
  TrustyAI-owned half of this requirement (service-side validation and
  support of the integration).
